name: Lexus 1LR-GUE 4.8 L V10 (LFA, 2010-2012)
summary: A 72-degree V10 with one shared crank pin per cylinder pair, so it fires evenly every 72 degrees. Ten individual throttles, a tuned surge tank, equal-length exhaust manifolds and a 9,000 rpm limit give it the smooth, high-pitched wail it is known for.

rod_length_mm.note: Not found. Rods are forged titanium (australiancar.reviews, ja.wikipedia).

firing_order.note: Not found on any page opened. Cylinder numbering and bank assignment also not found.

crank.value: One crank pin carries one piston from each bank (five shared pins, no split pins). Forged, nitrided Ni-Cr-Mo steel, fully counterweighted. Main journal 62 mm x 24 mm, pin 45 mm x 31 mm, stroke 79 mm, mass 18,670 g.
crank.note: Motor Fan article on the 1LR-GUE crankshaft, citing the maker Aichi Steel. Material from ja.wikipedia. Pin phase angles are not printed; with a 72-degree bank and shared pins, even firing requires pins 72 degrees apart in firing sequence (my inference from the stated even firing).

firing_intervals_deg.note: Motor Fan: the 72-degree bank angle was chosen to give evenly spaced firing. 720/10 = 72 is my arithmetic. en.wikipedia's Lexus LFA page also calls it even-firing.

valves_per_cylinder.note: 40-valve DOHC, rocker-arm type. Titanium intake and exhaust valves; rocker lever ratio about 1; included valve angle about 25 degrees (ja.wikipedia).

intake_duration_deg.note: Not found. Dual VVT-i (intake and exhaust phasing) per australiancar.reviews.

redline_rpm.note: Owner's manual 'Maximum Engine Speed 9,000 rpm'. en.wikipedia adds a fuel cut-off at 9,500 rpm (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota_LR_engine), which I could not confirm in a Toyota document.

peak_torque_rpm.note: Sources disagree: the US owner's manual and Motor Fan say 7,000 rpm; Toyota's 21 Oct 2009 launch release and en.wikipedia say 6,800 rpm (https://web.archive.org/web/20100211113226/http://www2.toyota.co.jp/en/news/09/10/1021.html). 90% of peak torque is available from 3,700 to 9,000 rpm (both Toyota documents).

intake_type.value: individual throttles (10 electronically controlled throttle bodies) fed from an acoustically tuned surge tank; short runners with curled air funnels inside the surge tank; dual intake path that switches from a primary inlet port to dual ports at higher speed
intake_type.note: Throttles and tuned surge tank from Toyota's release; funnel detail from ja.wikipedia; port switching from australiancar.reviews.

header_type.value: equal-length manifold runners, one manifold per bank (5-into-1 is not stated), into an equal-length dual exhaust
header_type.note: Toyota: 'Equal-length exhaust manifolds combined with an equal-length dual exhaust system routed through a multistage titanium main muffler'.

exhaust_notes.value: Titanium dual-stage rear silencer with a valve; above about 3,000 rpm the valve opens and the sound-deadening chambers are bypassed.
exhaust_notes.note: Same 3,000 rpm valve behaviour described by km77 (https://www.km77.com/coches/lexus/lfa/2010/coupe/informacion/lexus-lfa-motor-y-bastidor-informacion-tecnica).

missing: runner, throttle and exhaust primary dimensions

sources.what: Toyota-hosted 2011 Lexus LFA owner's manual (US). Manufacturer document; has the engine specification table.
Toyota global press release of 21 Oct 2009 announcing the LFA (archived). Manufacturer; power, torque, intake and exhaust description.
Motor Fan (Japanese technical magazine) article on the 1LR-GUE crankshaft with dimensions and the shared-pin layout.
Motor Fan engine profile of the 1LR-GUE; states the bank angle was chosen for even firing; spec table.
australiancar.reviews engine article; secondary summary of Lexus technical material (valvetrain, intake, exhaust).
Japanese Wikipedia article on the LR engine; more mechanical detail than the English page, but unreferenced in places.
English Wikipedia Toyota LR engine page; used only for the 9,500 rpm fuel cut and the 6,800 rpm torque figure.
km77 (Spanish car magazine) technical description of the LFA; exhaust valve behaviour.

name.note: 2011 LFA owner's manual (US), technical information pp.108-112; the 1LR-GUE's only car.

curb_kg.note: Quote: "Curb Weight 1,480 kg-1,590 kg*" / "*: Figures vary according to equipment and destination." Lower bound used. Toyota's 2009 release (https://global.toyota/en/detail/308263) gives "Vehicle weight" "1,480 kg." Wikipedia's 1,614 kg was not verified.

gear_count.note: Quote: "Transaxle Type ASG (Automated Sequential Gearbox)", "Transaxle Model RB60M".

final_drive.note: Quotes: "Front Counter Gear Ratio* 1.259" and "Differential Gear Ratio 3.417". 1.259 x 3.417 = 4.302 (ours). Check (ours): at 9,000 rpm this gives about 83 km/h in 1st, matching the manual's "1st 83 km/h" maximum permissible speed; without the counter gear it would not.

wheel_radius_m.note: Estimated (ours): rolling radius taken as 98% of the unloaded radius computed from the tyre size (rim diameter / 2 + section width x aspect ratio).

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'Lexus LFA' (read 2026-11-17), infobox layout: Front mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive.
